rejectedSkills.reason: Passes the rubric (9) -- concrete, self-contained, no broken links -- but not selected within the cap of 6. Instructions prioritise usability testing, evaluation, research, and registry gaps; usability-testing, synthetic-user-testing, research-planning, cognitive-accessibility, inclusive-personas, and accessible-content scored as high or higher and fill clearer gaps. Overlaps registry's better-accessibility (motion sensitivity) and theme-factory (dark mode/theming).

Its process requires assigning named Designpowers subagents (design-strategist, design-lead, content-writer, motion-designer, accessibility-reviewer, design-scout, defined in agents/*.md) as debate advocates -- a hard functional dependency on subagent definitions that live outside any single skill directory and cannot be meaningfully bundled without pulling in the whole agent roster. Not selected within the cap regardless.

Near-duplicate of the already-vendored design-debt-audit (from the same author's Owl-Listener/designer-skills repo) -- both maintain a register of deferred Minor/Note findings with severity, status, and escalation rules. Also functionally requires a shared design-state.md file maintained across the whole Designpowers pipeline, which this single skill does not carry.

Its first instruction is a 'Welcome Gate' that requires invoking using-designpowers (a 46KB, plugin-wide onboarding/routing document) before doing anything, and it mandates creating design-state.md, a shared file every other Designpowers skill reads/writes. Not self-contained as a standalone skill outside the full pipeline; conformance fails for hard-wired dependency on other repo infrastructure not bundled.

This is an onboarding/UX skill for the Designpowers plugin's own terminal experience (a 'first-time user' quick-win on-ramp with a mascot and a scripted welcome), not a general product-design skill an agent would use on a user's actual product. Low relevance for this registry.

Id collision: this session already vendors design-handoff from anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins (design/skills/design-handoff), which is a cleaner standalone generator with no pipeline coupling. This designpowers version covers similar ground (component specs, accessibility checklist, rationale) but is written to follow designpowers-critique and feed verification-before-shipping specifically, so it was not chosen to replace the other.

Its core function is fetching arbitrary community-authored DESIGN.md files at runtime from an external repo (VoltAgent/awesome-design-md) and loading them into the project -- the skill's own text calls this fetched content 'a prompt-injection surface' requiring runtime sanitisation. This is a live, unreviewed external content dependency at every invocation, not something that can be pinned and reviewed line-by-line the way the brief requires; also bundles a local library-index.md that would need to be kept in sync with a live upstream.

Overlaps the registry's already-vendored extract-design-md (stitch-extract-design-md), which covers reading and building from the same Google Labs/Stitch DESIGN.md format. This version adds a useful untrusted-data security framing but is otherwise a near-duplicate utility rather than a distinct design-work skill.

This is the agent's own cross-project behavioural memory system (writes to ~/.designpowers/taste-profile.md, explicitly never applied to steer design output) -- infrastructure for the Designpowers plugin's personalisation feature, not a skill that produces a design artefact. Also gated behind the using-designpowers Welcome Gate.

Reads extensively from design-state.md (decisions log, handoff chain, Design Debt Register) and writes into design-memory's taste-profile.md -- both shared pipeline files not present when this skill is vendored alone. Functionally incomplete without the rest of the Designpowers system.

Id collision with the already-vendored registry skill design-review (from plugin87/ux-ui-agent-skills, rubric total 8). This designpowers version also dispatches three non-vendored subagents (design-critic, accessibility-reviewer, heuristic-evaluator) in parallel per the Reconciliation Protocol defined in using-designpowers -- a hard external-agent dependency, on top of the naming collision.

This is the shared living-state-file protocol that every other Designpowers skill reads from and writes to (design-state.md) -- plumbing for the multi-agent pipeline, not itself a skill that produces design work. Also gated behind the using-designpowers Welcome Gate.

Solid, largely self-contained content (competitive-analysis table, principle-writing rules, experience mapping, success metrics) but not selected within the cap of 6 -- general strategy work, not the stated priority of testing/evaluation/research/gaps, and it carries a Welcome Gate reference to using-designpowers.

Overlaps the registry's already-vendored design-tokens, design-system-governance, and token-build, covering the same three-layer token model, component-spec documentation, naming conventions, and accessibility audit checklist. Not selected given the cap and this overlap.

A well-written aesthetic-calibration process, but deeply specific to the Designpowers pipeline's own taste-profile.md / DESIGN.md interplay (Welcome Gate, writes into design-state.md, referenced by name-specific agents like design-lead and motion-designer). Not selected given the cap and the instruction's priority on testing/evaluation/research/gaps rather than taste calibration.

Its own description says to use this 'instead of the Superpowers design-critique when working within a Designpowers workflow' -- an explicit pipeline-specific override, not a general-purpose skill. Overlaps the registry's critique-information-density and design-review cluster, and calls design-debt-tracker for deferred findings.

Hard-wired to Figma MCP tools (get_design_context, use_figma, create_new_file, etc.) and explicitly requires invoking separate, non-vendored Figma skills (/figma-use, /figma-generate-design, /figma-code-connect) before any write. Overlaps the registry's already-vendored figma-integration. Undeclared-service and external-skill dependency.

Not-vendored-keeper: its core instruction is to 'dispatch the heuristic-evaluator agent (see agents/heuristic-evaluator.md)' -- a subagent definition that lives outside the skill directory and cannot resolve after vendoring a single skill folder. It also leans on the Reconciliation Protocol and Auto-Mode Safeguard defined in the 46KB using-designpowers document for its stated behaviour (e.g. pausing on critical H1/H3 findings). Bundling just the one referenced file would not make the skill functionally complete, since its critical-path behaviour depends on protocols documented elsewhere.

Reasonable aesthetic-reference-gathering skill, but lower priority than the six selected (not testing, evaluation, research, or a clear registry gap) and its search step implicitly assumes web-browsing capability that isn't declared. Not selected within the cap.

Solid, self-contained state/feedback/error/motion/gesture guidance, but overlaps the registry's better-interface, design-details, and animate cluster for interaction and motion craft. Not selected within the cap of 6.

Near-duplicate of the already-vendored motion-system (from the same author's Owl-Listener/designer-skills repo) -- both cover animation duration/easing guides and mandatory reduced-motion alternatives. Skipped per the explicit instruction to avoid near-duplicates of the ten already-vendored designer-skills.

Decent, self-contained breakpoint/typography/touch-target guidance, but overlaps the registry's platform-conventions and better-layout, and is noticeably thinner (2.2KB) than the comparable ui-composition or better-layout content. Not selected within the cap.

A mid-build checkpoint mechanic that only makes sense embedded in the Designpowers build pipeline -- it reads the taste profile and design-state.md to decide checkpoint frequency and records signals into design-memory. Not functional as a standalone atomic skill.

Reads and synthesises the PERSONAL taste profile maintained by design-memory (~/.designpowers/taste-profile.md); without that accumulated file this skill has nothing to report on, so it is not functional standalone.
Near-duplicate of the registry's already-vendored design-tokens and token-build -- same three-layer global/semantic/component model, same naming-convention pattern, same dark-mode-as-remap approach.

Solid, self-contained visual-design guidance (layout, colour, typography, responsive, documentation), but overlaps the registry's better-colors, better-typography, better-layout, and laws-of-ux cluster heavily enough that it adds little beyond what those already cover. Not selected within the cap.

A 46KB master onboarding, welcome-sequence, and routing document for the whole Designpowers plugin ('MUST run before any other Designpowers skill') -- infrastructure for this repo's own multi-agent pipeline, not an atomic design-work skill in the sense this registry vendors.

Passes the rubric (9) -- concrete evidence-before-assertions checklist, structured report -- but not selected within the cap of 6 in favour of accessible-content, which scored uniqueness 2 (fills a clearer registry gap) versus this skill's uniqueness 1 (overlaps the registry's pre-handoff-review readiness gate).
Near-duplicate of the registry's already-vendored ux-writing -- both define voice attributes, tone-by-context, vocabulary do/don't lists, and reading-level targets for interface copy.

A reasonable task-breakdown skill (structure/component/layout/interaction/content/accessibility task categories, 2-5 minute task sizing, verification criteria per task), but it is closer to general project planning than a design-specific activity, and was not selected within the cap given the instruction's priority on testing/evaluation/research/gaps.
